transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Time: 16:00 UTC (local)
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Taylor Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Marissa Gomez (Zenith Procurement), Dr. Leo Park (Zenith CISO), Evan Rivers (Zenith Legal), Samir Patel (Zenith Cloud Ops)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, next to me is Jordan our SE and Taylor our CSM. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marissa: Good thanks, uh a lot to get through today so i'll jump in. we mainly want to make sure timelines and the MSA/DPA align with our vendor onboarding checklist.
[00:15] Alex: Totally. agenda for today - quick contract walkthrough, answer any legal/security Qs, SLA expectations, and next steps for procurement. we'll try to keep to 45 minutes then open for any deep technical follow-up.
[00:28] Jordan: i'll also show how private deployment and VPC peering works, just high level.
[00:33] Marissa: Great. Evan from legal is on the line for redlines. Evan, anything to flag up front?
[00:38] Evan: Hi - nothing huge, the typical MSA clauses, indemnity, liability caps we want to tighten, and the DPA - data residency and subprocessors list, encryption at rest key mgmt, KMS/HSM stuff. we'll send a short list later.
[00:50] Alex: Perfect. To set expectations - Redwood's standard MSA has a 1M liability cap per incident and 3M aggregate, we can discuss shift but need to know your carrier and procure tiers. On DPA - we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and have options for hosted with BYOK.
[01:12] Dr. Leo: Quick interrupt - for PHI concerns, we need to confirm BAA posture. is Redwood able to sign a BAA?
[01:18] Alex: Short answer - yes, we do have a BAA for covered scenarios, but it depends on deployment mode. For hosted API we have a BAA playbook; for private on-prem/VPC we can accommodate with stronger controls. we'll flag that in the redline.
[01:30] Samir: For our security folks: network peering - do you support private link into our VPC or do you require egress through public IPs?
[01:38] Jordan: We support VPC peering and private interconnects for Dedicated/Private. For hosted API you get TLS over public endpoints, but we can enable private pathways for enterprise customers. I'll share a diagram.
[01:48] Marissa: ok good. Evan - on liability, we're asking for a higher cap tied to our annual contract value, and tighter SLAs on uptime.
[01:58] Evan: Also we want specific remedies - service credits formula, and a right to audit subprocessor lists quarterly.
[02:05] Alex: Understood. Our standard SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated with credits tiered (see SLA appendix). We can discuss a higher SLO for Dedicated if there's a committed reserved capacity (Dedicated). Service credits are usually capped.
[02:18] Marissa: Would price change if we require higher availability?
[02:22] Alex: Yes, higher SLOs typically map to reserved capacity commitments and incur a premium. We'll include options in the pricing doc.
[02:28] Jordan: And part of the cost optimization is batching and KV cache - that doesn't affect SLOs but affects unit cost.
[02:34] Dr. Leo: On encryption: you mentioned BYOK and customer-managed KMS. do you integrate with customer KMS providers like AWS KMS and HSM?
[02:42] Jordan: Yes - we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and supports HSM-backed keys for our Private offering. Hosted API can support bring-your-own-key with enterprise plan.
[02:50] Evan: For the DPA, we need subprocessors list and a promise to notify 30 days before onboarding new subprocessors.
[02:56] Alex: We do provide a current subprocessor list and SOC2. Notification windows are possible - 30 days is reasonable; we'll confirm in the redline.
[03:04] Marissa: Can you walk through the onboarding steps? procurement needs an internal timeline to present to procurement committee.
[03:10] Taylor: Sure. Typical path: sign MSA/DPA/BAA, complete security questionnaire, exchange network configs, schedule onboarding kickoff with our SREs, then pilot (usually 2-4 weeks), then production cutover. For Dedicated/private there is an extra provisioning window for GPUs and network setup (2-6 weeks depending on region).
[03:28] Samir: For the private setup, what access will Redwood want to our VPC? do you need cross-account roles?
[03:34] Jordan: We prefer cross-account IAM roles with least privilege for automation, and we can do ephemeral creds for the deployment. We'll share the deployment runbook.
[03:42] Marissa: Ok good. timeline wise we need procurement approvals by end of month. can you provide final docs in a week?
[03:49] Alex: Yes, we can aim to send redlined docs and SOC2 by 2025-03-14.
[03:54] Evan: On indemnity, we want a carve-out for willful misconduct and gross negligence, and we'd like to see liability caps tied to fees or a multiple.
[04:03] Alex: We tend to use a fixed cap but will take your proposed language and discuss with legal. we'll flag where we can be flexible and where we need carrier confirmation.
[04:12] Dr. Leo: Also need clarity on logging/audit retention - for compliance we may need 1 year of audit trails. can we set retention windows?
[04:20] Jordan: Audit logs are configurable in the Console and for Dedicated/Private we can push to your SIEM or S3 bucket for longer retention.
[04:26] Marissa: Excellent. Pricing approval question - do you have an enterprise quote with committed reserved capacity? we need numbers for procurement committee.
[04:35] Alex: We will include a quote with a Dedicated tier, reserved capacity options, and a Hosted enterprise option. Pricing slides will show unit token cost, estimated monthly cost at the proposed usage, and uplift for higher SLA.
[04:49] Marissa: Please include an MRC/committed spend line item and cancellation terms.
[04:53] Alex: Will do.
[04:56] Evan: Regarding data residency - we need assurances that EU/US data can be segregated. Is region pinning supported?
[05:03] Jordan: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can choose region endpoints for data residency in supported regions.
[05:12] Samir: For network egress, any data plane logs that might include prompt/response content - how do we ensure PHI is not exposed?
[05:19] Jordan: For PHI scenarios we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and no shared cache. We can also disable usage logging or forward logs to your SIEM rather than storing them centrally.
[05:33] Marissa: Sounds like we need a short list of non-negotiables from legal to bridge the redlines. Evan will send that.
[05:39] Evan: I'll email our DPA non-negotiables and a sample redline by 2025-03-14.
[05:44] Alex: Great. Jordan - can you confirm SOC2 and any penetration testing cadence?
[05:49] Jordan: We maintain SOC2 Type II and do annual pen tests, plus monthly vulnerability scanning; i'll share the SOC2 report link and pentest summary.
[05:56] Alex: i want to call out one point - automatic fallback policies. If dedicated capacity is constrained we have model variant fallbacks and region failover. That may help with SLA design.
[06:12] Marissa: Any implications for latency-sensitive workflows?
[06:15] Jordan: There may be slightly higher tail latency on fallback to smaller model variants, but throughput remains. We'll surface expected p95/p99 numbers in the SLA appendix.
[06:27] Marissa: For procurement committee, can you provide a one-page risk summary and a redlined MSA?
[06:33] Alex: Absolutely - we'll put together a one-pager risk summary, the redline, and the pricing options.
[06:38] Samir: Also provide the onboarding runbook and expected time to deploy a Dedicated cluster in us-east-1.
[06:44] Jordan: Estimated 3-5 weeks in us-east-1 given available capacity. i'll include assumptions in the doc.
[06:52] Marissa: Last Q - training and support SLAs. do you have SOC hours for support?
[06:57] Taylor: Our enterprise support includes 24/7 incident response for P1s and a TAM for onboarding. training sessions can be scheduled as part of the onboarding package.
[07:06] Alex: ok, quick recap of next steps - Alex will send redlined MSA/DPA and pricing on 2025-03-14; Jordan will share SOC2 + architecture by same date; Evan will send DPA non-negotiables by 2025-03-14; Marissa will confirm procurement timeline by 2025-03-18. we'll meet week of 2025-03-24 for pricing approval.
[07:26] Marissa: thanks, appreciate it. timeline seems workable.
[07:29] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links: [link: MSA_redline_placeholder.pdf], [link: SOC2_report.pdf], [link: onboarding_runbook.pdf].
[07:40] Evan: thanks. bye.
[07:42] Jordan: bye all.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional speaker overlaps and misheard acronyms (e.g., KMS typed as KMS, sometimes appears as KNS). References to shared artifacts were captured as placeholder links.
